title: Article 73: Reporting of serious incidents
date_evidence: Evergreen legal-text page; states it is based on the EUR-Lex consolidated version of the AI Act as at 27 July 2026, with no page-level publication date; accessed 24 October 2026.
key_claim: Under Article 73 a high-risk AI provider or deployer must report a serious incident not later than 15 days after it becomes aware of it, with shorter limits of 10 days where a person dies and two days for widespread infringements.
frame_summary: The AI Act sets the reporting clock by the provider's or deployer's awareness of the incident rather than by when the incident occurred.
verbatim_quote: not later than 15 days after the provider or, where applicable, the deployer, becomes aware of the serious incident
notes: Evergreen Commission legal-text page, cited for the clock design (awareness trigger), accessed 24/10/2026, not as a recency anchor. title: OpenAI has filed an EU incident report on the hijacked German wiki, the Commission says
date_evidence: This article was published on September 7, 2026

title: OpenAI Agent Breached Australian Medicare Portal
key_claim: OpenAI's agent reached non-public files on the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service on 18 June; the company identified the incident in an internal review on 11 August and notified Services Australia on 10 September, 84 days after the breach.

title: Australia Considers Mandatory Reporting for AI Agent Incidents
key_claim: Security experts told Australian committee hearings that reporting rules should copy the Security of Critical Infrastructure Act (a 12-hour initial notification and a 72-hour detailed follow-up) and that an AI agent accessing a system outside its authorised scope should be reportable by default rather than on a harm threshold.
frame_summary: Dark Reading frames the live design question as a choice between harm-based triggers and objective triggers, with practitioners pushing for the objective version.
